title: Gluing K-flat tensor comparisons along a stupid tail
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. Let Q be a cochain complex of R-modules and k an integer with Q^n=0 for n<k. Set T=\sigma_{\ge k+1}Q (the stupid truncation) and S=Q^k[-k] (the one-term complex). Suppose that for each of S and T, every quasi-isomorphism g:F\to S or g:F\to T with F K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] remains a quasi-isomorphism after termwise tensoring with B. Then for every K-flat P and quasi-isomorphism f:P\to Q, the termwise tensor map f\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism. No upper bound or Tor hypothesis is imposed on Q.

source.place: Section 15.60, Lemmas 15.60.7, 15.60.9, 15.60.12 and Definition 15.60.13; parent Tag 08IB final affine calculation

proof.text: Put T=sigma_{>=k+1}Q and S=Q^k[-k]. Since Q vanishes below k, the inclusion T -> Q and the projection Q -> S form a degreewise split short exact sequence. Its connecting map S -> T[1] is d^k with the shift sign. Tensoring with B preserves the split term sequences and gives the corresponding distinguished triangle [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle].

On K(R), termwise tensor followed by localization is triangulated. K-flat objects form a resolving class: use the functorial flat resolutions of ordinary ModuleCat in the source KFlat library. Quasi-isomorphisms between them remain invertible after tensoring by [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-kflat-quasi-iso] for the identity ring map and B[0]. Apply the generic [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to obtain the exact derived tensor and its comparison counit, computed on every K-flat resolution. Shifts of resolutions and the termwise tensor-shift identifications make this counit shift-compatible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] to obtain a morphism from the derived-tensor triangle of T,Q,S to the ordinary-tensor triangle of the same split sequence.

The hypotheses give isomorphisms for all cohomology maps on T and S. The triangle morphism gives a cohomology ladder [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder]. In each five-term segment the four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms; [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] gives the middle isomorphism. Model independence identifies the middle comparison with the image of the specified f tensor B, so it is a quasi-isomorphism.

theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_stupid_tail
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (k : ℤ)
    (hbelow : ∀ n : ℤ, n < k → IsZero (Q.X n))
    (hsingle : ∀ (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R))
      (f : P.obj ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} R)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) k).obj (Q.X k)), QuasiIso f →
      QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f))
    (htail : ∀ (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R))
      (f : P.obj ⟶ Q.stupidTrunc (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntGE (k + 1))), QuasiIso f →
      QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f))
    (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q)
    (hf : QuasiIso f) :
    QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
